Project Learning

-> We don’t store user-uploaded data on the production server because of limited storage, scaling issues, and reliability concerns. Instead, we use cloud storage providers like AWS S3 or Google Cloud Storage, which give us scalable, secure, and globally accessible storage.


-> In backend development, we often use sensitive credentials like database URLs and API keys. If someone gains access to these, they can compromise the whole app. To prevent this, we store such data in a separate .env file, and load them securely as environment variables instead of hardcoding them in the codebase. On requireng the en variables we use config that is the correct use of the env variables bcoz config read the env file and use the variables in process.env


-> in the production we dosent create all the api in the server.js or app.js file we have to made an separate folder to make api's. we need again require the express 

-> when we use the another folder for creating an api then we have to export that variable from that file and need to require in the app.js file using the middleware and we use app.use('/',songRoute) it says that we makes an api in the routes folder so from there you have to use the api

-> in the creating api and giving data to the website we know the if the data is in string format then we all go body raw format but if we giving the file then we have to use the key value pair and we have to use form-data.

-> when we have the form-data then why we use thr raw format bcoz when we use the raw format then we having the less recourses to read the data, while in form-data we having high resources to read the data. we also use the binary format to upload the files 

-> if we use the body raw format then it doesn't read the value or data by default that's why we have to use the express.json() which was the middleware , but if we talk about the form-data then we have to use same thing with the form-data but here middleware doesn't work and that's why we use the multer were it is a package

-> const upload = multer({storage:multer.memoryStorage()}); // here multer is use the temprory memory storage to store the files for reading

-> router.post("/songs",upload.single("audio"),(req,res)=>{}) : here "audio" name used bcoz when we enter the file the whatever we give the key name of the file then same given here too, if there is a multiple files then we have to use array instead of single

-> access the file we use the req.file

-> res.status(201).json({}) : here we use 201 means its is a status code where its mean is that api is generating an new resource
